context: Output of tools/analyze_state_noise_capture.py against the 10s/4730-sample stationary capture (capture_20260728_154018.jsonl). This is the empirical false-positive noise floor of CartesianMoveMonitor's own speed/accel formulas, computed from real consecutive stationary samples with real measured dt -- no assumed nominal dt_s involved.
key_finding: The CartesianMoveMonitor accel check's historical thresholds (0.2/0.5 m/s^2 defaults) were derived from MuJoCo simulation, which has zero sensor noise. Real RTDE telemetry at 500Hz, double-differenced (speed = step_m/dt, accel = |speed_i - speed_{i-1}|/dt), has a noise floor with MEDIAN reading 1.74 m/s^2 while stationary -- already ~3.5x the default 0.5 threshold. This retroactively explains all direct_torque-mode first-cycle trips observed 2026-07-28 (0.58, 0.62, 1.07, 2.29, 2.30 m/s^2 across several trials, all with negligible real qd/tau/drift) as normal noise, not real problems. Distinguishable from the one genuinely real issue found the same day (position-mode wrist-singularity divergence) by the presence/absence of real, growing qd alongside the accel reading.
caveat: Single pose/dynamics_source/frequency (direct_torque local dynamics, height_alpha=0.5-ish region, wrist_2=0.1). Not yet confirmed whether this noise floor generalizes across poses, control rates, or dynamics_source=rtde -- re-capture at other configurations before trusting this distribution there.
